Order (As per Sri R.LakshmiNarasimha Rao, Honble Member).
*** 

 

  

 

The opposite party No.1 is the appellant. The appeal is
challenge to the order dated 30-4-2013 passed by the District Forum in C.C.No.42/2012 whereby
the appellant and respondent No.2 were directed to pay to the complainant a sum
of Rs.3,800/- towards the cost of the phone together with compensation of
Rs.500/- and costs of Rs.500/-.
The facts leading to filing of the appeal are that the respondent
No.1 purchased a CELKON -9 Mobile phone from the appellant for a sum of
Rs.3,800/- along with Memory card for Rs.250/- under warranty for total sale
consideration of Rs.4,050/-. Due to
manufacturing defects, the colour of the screen of the mobile phone faded and
became ugly. The respondent approached
the appellant along with the mobile phone for replacement and the appellant
refused to replace the mobile phone, therefore, the respondent filed
C.C.No.22/11 which was allowed by the
District Forum on 22-10-2011 by directing the appellant and the respondent No.2
to replace the Mobile phone with costs.
The appellant replaced the Mobile phone and also paid
costs in implementing the order of the District Forum. The respondent again approached the appellant
stating that the new mobile phone was also not functioning properly and it got
faded away and the voice is not audible and there was no proper response from
the appellant. The respondent got issued
notices dated 20-10-2012 and 0511-2012 and as the defect in the mobile phone
was not rectified, alleging deficiency in service, he filed the complaint
seeking direction to the appellant to pay an amount of Rs.3,800/- towards the
cost of the mobile phone together with Rs.20,000/- towards compensation.
The appellant filed written version resisting the
complaint. It contended that as per the
order in C.C.No.22/2011 dated 21-10-2011, it replaced the mobile phone with new
mobile phone on 24-11-2011. The
appellant denied the allegation that the new mobile phone has posed the same
problem and faded and that after the mobile phone is used for talking for 5 minutes, the voice becomes not in-audible
and he contended that the Mobile phone handed over to the respondent is a brand
new one and the problems pointed out by the respondent may be due to physical
damage to the mobile set and the appellant submitted that there is no
deficiency in service on its part and prayed for dismissal of the complaint.
The respondent filed his affidavit and relied on Exs.A1
to A7 and the Showroom Manager of appellant filed his affidavit.
The District Forum allowed the complaint on the premise
that there is deficiency in service on behalf of the appellants and directed
the appellant to pay to the respondent Rs.3,800/- i.e. the cost of the phone
together with compensation of Rs.500/- and costs of Rs.500/-.
Aggrieved by the order of the District Forum, the appellants
have filed appeal contending that the District Forum failed to see that the
Mobile Phone sold to the respondent No.1 was promptly replaced by them pursuant
to the orders in CC 22/2011 dated 21-10-2011 and that the same was used by the
respondent for more than 11 months without any complaint and only at the end of
the warranty period, he filed the C.C. 42/2012 with a dishonest intention to
get a new mobile phone.
The appellant contended that the respondent did not
make any allegations in his notices that the voice in the Mobile phone was not
audible and for the first time made the allegations in the complaint. The District Forum having observed that the mobile phone placed before it as
M.O.No.1 faded and has water marks, it ought
not have come to a conclusion that the mobile phone was defective without
sending it for expert opinion as required under
Section 13(1)(c)
of the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986 and prayed to dismiss the complaint.
The
respondent has sent written arguments by post.
The point for
consideration is whether the order of the District Forum suffers from mis-appreciation
of facts or law?
The respondent earlier filed complaint, C.C.No.22 of
2011 seeking for direction to the appellant to replace the mobile phone that he
purchased from the appellant on 24.11.2011 stated to have faded.
The District Forum allowed the complaint directing the appellant to
replace the mobile phone or return the cost of the phone with interest together
with compensation etc.,. Operative portion of the order reads as under:
In
the result, this complaint is allowed. The Opposite Parties Nos.1 

 

and
2 are directed jointly and severally either to replace the defective cellular
phone instrument or to refund the price of the instrument Rs.4,050/- (Rupees
Four Thousand Fifty only) together with interest at the rate of 9% per annum
from 07-05-2011 till payment. The Opposite Parties Nos.1 and 2 are further
directed to pay an amount of Rs.1,000/- (Rupees One Thousand only) towards
compensation and to pay a sum of Rs.500/- (Rupees Five Hundred only) towards
costs of the Complaint. The direction shall be complied with within 30 (thirty)
days from the date of receiving copy of this award. The Opposite Parties shall be at liberty to take the deposited
mobile M.O.1 along with connected Bill and Warranty Card, on compliance of the
award directions.
In
compliance of the order of the District Forum, the appellant replaced the
Celkon mobile phone with a new phone of the same model. The appellant replaced
the phone with a new mobile phone on 24.11.2011 and the respondent addressed
letter dated 20.10.2012 that new mobile phone also posed the problem that the
earlier phone did, viz, it faded and he issued another notice on 3.11.2012 with
the same demand, i.e. replacement of the phone with a new mobile phone.
The learned counsel for the
appellant has contended that the respondent did not make any complaint as
regards functioning of mobile phone for a period of 11 months and just before
expiry of warranty period he filed the complaint without depositing the mobile
phone and the District Forum created a case for the respondent even where there
are no pleading to the effect that mobile phone began to give trouble within
seven months of its purchase and the District Forum came to conclusion that the
mobile phone is defective even without getting it tested in a laboratory.
Admittedly, for 11 months after
the previously purchased mobile phone was replaced, the respondent has not
raised any complaint in regard to functioning of the mobile phone or fading of
its colour. The respondent in his notice dated 20.10.2012 and 3.11.2012 did
mention the only problem he faced with
the mobile phone is that it faded. The findings as to voice was not audible and the mobile phone started
giving trouble within seven months of its purchase does not find place in any
of the notices and as such we hold the observation made by the District Forum
in this regard is not based on any evidence.
The contention of the learned
counsel for the appellant that the respondent did not approach the appellant
till filing of the complaint cannot be accepted in the light of the notice
dated 20.10.2012 and 3.11.2012 which were sent with a request to replace the
mobile phone with a new mobile phone. The appellant failed to respond by giving
reply to the notice. However, the finding of the District Forum that the
appellants failure to give reply to the notice of the respondent amounts to
deficiency in service on the part of the appellant is not sustainable as it is settled position of law that mere failure
of a party to lis to give reply to the notice issued earlier cannot be made
criterion to find that party liable to comply with what is stated in the
notice. The finding of the District Forum in this regard is liable to be set
aside.
We find substance in the
contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that there was no complaint
from the respondent for a period of 11 months from the date of replacement of
the mobile phone as regard to functioning of the mobile phone and the District
Forum cannot come to a conclusion in absence of any report from laboratory as
to the defect in the mobile phone. The
mobile phone can be said to be water
logged in the light of the fact that as the District Forum returned finding
that it found water drops inside the glass of the mobile phone. The water
logged condition of the mobile phone by itself cannot be held as the sole
factor for mobile phone to get faded.
Taking all these facts into consideration, this
Commission comes to the conclusion that the respondent contributed to fading of
the colour of the mobile phone and the appellant for no manufacturing defect in
the mobile phone cannot be held liable to replace the mobile phone with a new mobile
phone. As there is also some degree of negligence on the part of the appellant
in not advising the respondent to take the mobile phone as to find the cause
for the mobile phone to get faded, we are of the opinion that the appellant is
entitled to compensation and costs awarded by the District Forum and not for
replacement of the mobile phone with a new mobile phone. Accordingly, the order
of the District Forum is liable to be modified.
In the result, the appeal is allowed. The order of the
District Forum is modified. The appellant/opposite party is directed to pay
compensation, a sum of Rs.500/- and costs of Rs.500/- to the respondent. There
shall be no separate order as to costs in the appeal. Time for compliance four
weeks.
